result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a high-visibility continental crosswalk and wide sidewalks, indicating a prioritized walking area. However, the multi-lane roadway and presence of parked vehicles near the crossing create potential visibility issues and long exposure times for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the left side of the street near the crosswalk obstruct the view between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Unprotected Multi-lane Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross three lanes of traffic plus a bike lane without a median or refuge island, increasing risk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, across the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Installing bulb-outs would shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight before they enter the travel lanes.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restricting parking within 20 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Adding a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image depicts a standard urban intersection featuring high-visibility continental crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals. The presence of 'No Turn on Red' signage and curb ramps indicates a baseline level of pedestrian-oriented design in a mixed-use environment.

hazards.name: Turning vehicle conflicts
hazards.description: Vehicles turning into the crosswalk from the intersecting street may conflict with pedestrians, particularly during the green phase.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve the visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Implement a signal timing change that gives pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban multi-lane street with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a dedicated bike lane. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the long crossing distance and parked vehicles near the intersection create visibility and exposure risks.

hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and well-maintained sidewalks. While the environment is generally supportive of pedestrians, the lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions leaves pedestrians exposed to turning traffic.

hazards.name: Turning Vehicle Conflicts
hazards.description: Vehicles turning from the cross street into the one-way street may conflict with pedestrians who have the walk signal.

hazards.name: Wide Corner Radii
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively fast vehicle turns, increasing the risk of high-impact collisions.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and increase pedestrian visibility.
